subject: maths
title: Symmetry: Lines of Symmetry and Rotational Symmetry
seo_title: Year 4 Symmetry Worksheets: Line and Rotational Symmetry (Free Maths, Answer Key)
standard_text: Recognise line and rotational symmetry of shapes and create symmetrical patterns and pictures, using dynamic geometric software where appropriate
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on symmetry for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4SP03): find lines of symmetry in shapes and letters, count mirror lines, complete symmetrical pictures on a grid, and recognise rotational symmetry and its order. Includes flags, road signs and nature. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Line symmetry: fold it and the halves match. Rotational symmetry: turn it and it looks the same before a full turn.
key_sub: A rectangle has 2 mirror lines, not 4. A parallelogram has no mirror lines but looks the same after a half turn (order 2). Order 1 means no rotational symmetry.
body_html:
What is a line of symmetry?

A line of symmetry (also called a mirror line) splits a shape into two halves that fit exactly on top of each other when you fold along it. Each half is a mirror image of the other.

To test a line, imagine folding the shape along it, or stand a small mirror on the line: if the reflection shows the whole shape, it is a mirror line.

Count every mirror line

Try every way to fold: up and down, across and slanting. A shape can have many mirror lines, one, or none. A regular shape (all sides and angles equal) has as many mirror lines as sides.

ShapeLines of symmetryOrder of rotational symmetry
Square44
Rectangle (not a square)22
Rhombus (not a square)2 (corner to corner)2
Parallelogram (slanting sides)02
Equilateral triangle33
Isosceles triangle11
Kite11
Isosceles trapezium11
Regular pentagon, hexagon, octagon5, 6, 85, 6, 8
CircleInfinitely manyInfinitely many

Complete a symmetrical picture

Give every shaded square a partner on the other side of the mirror line, the same number of squares away from the line. Count from the mirror line, not from the edge of the grid. Flip the half; do not slide it.

Rotational symmetry: does it look the same after a turn?

A shape has rotational symmetry if it looks exactly the same after a turn of less than a full turn about its centre. The order is how many times it looks the same during one full turn. Trace the shape on tracing paper, hold the centre with a pencil and turn it, or try it with geometry software.

Worked example

How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?

3 lines join opposite corners. 3 more join the middles of opposite sides. 3 + 3 = 6.

Answer: 6

Worked example

A parallelogram has no mirror lines. Does it have rotational symmetry?

Turn it a half turn about its centre. Each corner lands where the opposite corner was, so it fits exactly.

Answer: Yes, order 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting a rectangle’s diagonals as mirror linesFold on a diagonal: the corners stick out. A rectangle has 2
Saying a parallelogram has 2 mirror linesIts diagonals cut it in half, but the halves do not fit. It has 0
Mixing up mirror and turn symmetryMirror = fold, turn = rotate. A parallelogram has 0 mirror lines but order 2
Saying order 0Every shape looks the same after a full turn, so the smallest order is 1
Sliding the half when completing a pictureFlip it: each square goes the same distance on the other side
Forgetting colours on flags and signsColours must match too: the Aboriginal Flag has only 1 mirror line

faq.q: What do Year 4 students learn about symmetry in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 4 (AC9M4SP03) students Recognise line and rotational symmetry of shapes and create symmetrical patterns and pictures, sometimes using geometry software.

faq.q: What is the difference between line symmetry and rotational symmetry?
faq.a: A shape has line symmetry if it can be folded so the two halves match. It has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after a turn of less than a full turn, like a parallelogram after a half turn.

faq.q: Does a rectangle have 4 lines of symmetry?
faq.a: No. A rectangle that is not a square has 2 lines of symmetry: up and down, and across. Its diagonals split it in half, but the halves do not fit when folded.

faq.q: What does order of rotational symmetry mean?
faq.a: It is the number of times a shape looks exactly the same during one full turn. A square has order 4, a rectangle order 2, and a shape that only matches after a full turn has order 1.

items.q: Which dashed line is a mirror line?
items.e: Imagine folding each shape on its dashed line. Only in D does one half fit exactly on the other. Others: A: the line is not through the middle; B: equal parts, but they do not fit when folded; C: the line is not through the middle.

items.q: Which dashed line is not a mirror line?
items.e: In C the line splits the rectangle into 2 equal parts, but they do not fit when folded. In the other 3 pictures the halves fold exactly onto each other.
In B the line splits the parallelogram into 2 equal parts, but they do not fit when folded. In the other 3 pictures the halves fold exactly onto each other.

items.q: Which dashed line is a mirror line?
items.e: Imagine folding each shape on its dashed line. Only in A does one half fit exactly on the other. Others: B: the line is not through the middle; C: equal parts, but they do not fit when folded; D: the line is not through the middle. Remember: the diagonal of a rectangle splits it in half, but it is not a mirror line.

items.q: Which capital letter has a horizontal mirror line?
items.e: Fold E across the middle and the top arm lands on the bottom arm. M, T and V have a vertical mirror line instead.

items.q: Which capital letter has no mirror line?
items.e: F has no mirror line. H has 2, A has a vertical one and C has a horizontal one.

items.q: Which capital letter has 2 mirror lines?
items.e: X matches when folded up and down and when folded across. A and W have only a vertical line, and E only a horizontal one.
Fold Y straight down the middle and the 2 arms match. B, D and C have a horizontal line, not a vertical one.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
items.e: A square has 4 mirror lines: one up and down, one across and 2 along the diagonals, from corner to corner. Students often forget the diagonals.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle have?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 mirror lines: up and down, and across, through the middles of the sides. A diagonal splits it into 2 equal triangles, but they do not fit when folded, so the diagonals do not count.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle (3 equal sides) have?
items.e: Each mirror line goes from a corner to the middle of the side opposite. 3 corners, so 3 lines.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles triangle (2 equal sides) have?
items.e: Only the line from the top corner to the middle of the bottom side works: 1 line.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a scalene triangle (no equal sides) have?
items.e: The 3 sides are all different lengths, so no fold makes the halves fit. 0 lines of symmetry.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
items.e: Any straight line through the centre of a circle is a mirror line. You could never draw them all, so a circle has infinitely many.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus have?
items.e: This rhombus (not a square) has 2 mirror lines, both from corner to corner. Lines through the middles of the sides do not work.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram have?
items.e: A parallelogram with slanting sides has 0 mirror lines. Its diagonals and its middle lines split it into equal halves, but none of them fit when folded.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a kite have?
items.e: Only the line from the top corner to the bottom corner works, so a kite has 1 mirror line.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles trapezium have?
items.e: Only the up-and-down line through the middles of the top and bottom works. Folding across does not, because the top is shorter than the bottom: 1 line.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
items.e: Each mirror line goes from a corner to the middle of the side opposite. 5 corners, so 5 lines.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
items.e: 3 lines join opposite corners and 3 more join the middles of opposite sides: 3 + 3 = 6 lines.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular octagon have?
items.e: 4 lines join opposite corners and 4 join the middles of opposite sides: 4 + 4 = 8 lines.
Only the line straight up through the middle of the flat side works: 1 line. Folding across puts the curve on the flat side.
An oval has 2 mirror lines: one across the long way and one up and down. Slanting lines do not work, because it is not a circle.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this cross (all 4 arms the same) have?
items.e: Up and down and across both work, and so do the 2 slanting lines through the inside corners: 4 lines, just like a square.

items.q: Which shape has exactly 3 lines of symmetry?
items.e: Count the mirror lines of each shape: A (rectangle) 2 lines, B (isosceles triangle) 1 line, C (square) 4 lines, D (equilateral triangle) 3 lines. So the answer is D.

items.q: Which shape has no lines of symmetry?
items.e: Count the mirror lines of each shape: A (parallelogram) 0 lines, B (kite) 1 line, C (rectangle) 2 lines, D (rhombus) 2 lines. So the answer is A.

items.q: Which shape has the most lines of symmetry?
items.e: Count the mirror lines of each shape: A (regular hexagon) 6 lines, B (regular octagon) 8 lines, C (regular pentagon) 5 lines, D (square) 4 lines. So the answer is B.

items.q: Which shape has exactly 1 line of symmetry?
items.e: Count the mirror lines of each shape: A (parallelogram) 0 lines, B (rectangle) 2 lines, C (kite) 1 line, D (rhombus) 2 lines. So the answer is C.

items.q: The mirror line runs through the middle of a column. Shade squares to the right of the line to make the picture symmetrical. How many squares will be shaded altogether?
items.e: 10 squares are shaded now. 4 of them sit on the mirror line, so each is its own partner: count them once. The other 6 each need a partner. 6 + 6 + 4 = 16.

items.q: The mirror line runs through the middle of a row. Shade squares below the line to make the picture symmetrical. How many squares will be shaded altogether?
items.e: 12 squares are shaded now. 5 of them sit on the mirror line, so each is its own partner: count them once. The other 7 each need a partner. 7 + 7 + 5 = 19.

items.q: The mirror line runs through the middle of a column. How many more squares must be shaded to make the picture symmetrical?
items.e: Squares on the mirror line are their own partners. 10 squares are shaded and 4 sit on the line, so 10 − 4 = 6 more squares.

items.q: The mirror line runs through the middle of a row. How many more squares must be shaded to make the picture symmetrical?
items.e: Squares on the mirror line are their own partners. 13 squares are shaded and 6 sit on the line, so 13 − 6 = 7 more squares.

sets.title: Rotational symmetry: quarter turns, half turns and order

items.q: Turn this square about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: Turn a square a quarter turn and every side lands where another side was. It looks the same after a quarter turn (order 4).

items.q: Turn this rectangle about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: After a quarter turn the long sides stand up, so it looks different. After a half turn it is back the same (order 2). A quarter turn only works for a square.

items.q: Turn this equilateral triangle about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: 3 equal sides and 3 equal corners: each corner moves to where the next one was after a third of a turn (order 3). After a half turn it points down, so a half turn does not work.

items.q: Turn this kite about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: A kite has a mirror line, but turning it always moves the sharp top corner somewhere else until it has gone all the way round. It has no rotational symmetry (order 1).

items.q: Turn this parallelogram about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: A parallelogram has no mirror lines, but after a half turn it fits exactly on itself (order 2). Do not mix up mirror symmetry and turn symmetry.

items.q: Turn this plus sign about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: All 4 arms are the same, so after a quarter turn each arm lands where the next arm was (order 4).

items.q: Turn this isosceles triangle about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: It has a mirror line down the middle, but any turn less than a full turn moves the top corner to a new place. Only a full turn works (order 1).

items.q: Turn this pinwheel shape about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: Each blade lands on the next blade after a quarter turn (order 4). This shape has no mirror lines at all, because the blades all lean the same way.

items.q: Turn this rhombus about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: All 4 sides are equal, but it is not a square: after a quarter turn the long diagonal lies across, so it looks different. After a half turn it fits exactly (order 2).

items.q: Turn this trapezium about its centre (the dot). What is the smallest turn that makes it look exactly the same as before?
items.e: After a half turn the short side is at the bottom, so it looks different. Only a full turn works (order 1), even though it has a mirror line.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a square?
items.e: A square looks the same after 1, 2, 3 and 4 quarter turns. Order 4.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle looks the same after a half turn and after a full turn: 2 times in one full turn, so order 2.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of an equilateral triangle?
items.e: It looks the same after each third of a turn: 3 times in one full turn. Order 3.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a regular hexagon?
items.e: Each corner moves to the next corner after a sixth of a turn, so it looks the same 6 times in a full turn. Order 6.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a parallelogram?
items.e: It has 0 mirror lines, but it looks the same after a half turn and a full turn. Order 2. The number of mirror lines and the order of rotational symmetry are different things.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a kite?
items.e: A kite only looks the same after a full turn. That counts once, so the order is 1, not 0. Order 1 means it has no rotational symmetry.

items.q: Which shape looks exactly the same after a half turn?
items.e: Order of rotational symmetry: A (equilateral triangle) 3, B (parallelogram) 2, C (isosceles triangle) 1, D (kite) 1. Only B fits on itself after a half turn.

items.q: Which shape looks exactly the same after a quarter turn?
items.e: Order of rotational symmetry: A (square) 4, B (regular hexagon) 6, C (rhombus) 2, D (rectangle) 2. Only A fits on itself after a quarter turn.

items.q: Which shape has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry?
items.e: Check both kinds of symmetry: A (rectangle) 2 lines, order 2, B (kite) 1 line, order 1, C (pinwheel) 0 lines, order 4, D (trapezium) 1 line, order 1. Only C turns onto itself but has no mirror line.

items.q: Which capital letter looks exactly the same after a half turn (upside down)?
items.e: Turn the page upside down: N is still N. E, A and T have a mirror line, but upside down they look different.

sets.title: Symmetry in Australian life: flags, signs, nature and art

items.e: Only the line straight down the body works: each wing lands on the wing opposite. Folded across, the big top wings would land on the small bottom wings. 1 line.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this leaf have?
items.e: Fold along the middle vein: the veins on each side match. Folded across, the stalk has nothing to match, so there is just 1 line.

items.q: The Australian Aboriginal Flag has a black top half, a red bottom half and a yellow circle in the centre. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Fold it up and down: black lands on black, red on red and the circle on itself. Fold it across: black lands on red, so that is not a mirror line. Colours must match too. 1 line.

items.q: This plain flag has a white cross through the middle. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Fold it up and down or across: the cross lands on itself both times. The diagonals do not work, because the flag is a rectangle, not a square. 2 lines.

items.q: A STOP sign has this shape. Without the word STOP, how many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: It is a regular octagon: 4 lines join opposite corners and 4 join the middles of opposite sides. 8 lines. (With the word STOP on it, it would have none.)

items.q: A GIVE WAY sign is a triangle pointing down like this. Without the words, how many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: It is an equilateral triangle, just upside down. Each mirror line goes from a corner to the middle of the side opposite: 3 lines.

items.q: Many Australian warning signs are yellow diamonds like this one. With no picture inside, how many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: This diamond is a square standing on a corner. A square has 4 mirror lines: corner to corner up and down and across, and 2 slanting lines through the middles of the sides.

items.q: A NO ENTRY sign is a red circle with a white bar across it. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: A plain circle has infinitely many, but the bar spoils most of them. Only the line across and the line up and down keep the bar on itself: 2 lines.

items.q: The big white star on the Australian flag, the Commonwealth Star, has 7 points like this star. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Each mirror line goes from a point through the centre to the gap between 2 points on the other side. 7 points, so 7 lines. (14 counts every corner, inside and outside, but each line passes through 2 of them.)

items.q: A sea star (starfish) at the beach has 5 arms, like this picture. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Each mirror line runs down the middle of one arm and between the 2 arms opposite. 5 arms, so 5 lines.

items.q: This dot pattern is in a style used in many Aboriginal artworks: a circle in the centre with 6 dots around it. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: 3 lines pass through pairs of opposite dots and 3 more pass between the dots. 6 lines. It is round, but the dots spoil the other lines, so it does not have infinitely many.

items.q: Cooper looks at the Australian National Flag. It has the Union Jack in the top-left corner and white stars on blue. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: The Union Jack is only in the top-left corner. Any fold puts it on top of blue and stars, so the halves never match: 0 lines.

items.q: Amelia has a square paper napkin. In how many different ways can she fold it in half so that the two halves match exactly?
items.e: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: up and down, across, and the 2 diagonals. So there are 4 ways.

items.q: Lachlan folds a picnic rug, 2 m long and 1 m wide, from one corner to the opposite corner. Do the two halves match?
c: No, it has no mirror lines
items.e: The diagonal splits the rug into 2 equal triangles, but they do not fit on top of each other, because it is not a square. A rectangle has only 2 mirror lines.

items.q: Isla says a parallelogram has 2 lines of symmetry because its diagonals cut it in half. Is she right?
items.e: Cutting a shape in half is not enough: the halves must fit when folded. Fold a slanting parallelogram any way and the corners stick out, so it has 0 lines of symmetry. (It does look the same after a half turn.)

items.q: Oliver writes words in capital letters. Which word has a horizontal mirror line?
items.e: C, O, D and E each have a horizontal mirror line, so a fold across the middle of the whole word CODE works. T, Y and A only have vertical lines, and S and N have none.

items.q: Ruby cuts out a paper circle. How many different fold lines will make the two halves match?
items.e: Every line through the centre of a circle is a line of symmetry, so there are infinitely many. Up and down, across and the 2 diagonals are just 4 of them.

items.q: Matilda folds a sheet of paper in half, cuts a shape along the fold and opens it out. What must be true?
c: The fold is a mirror line
items.e: Both halves were cut at the same time, so each is the mirror image of the other. The fold is always a line of symmetry. The shape might have other mirror lines too, but it does not have to.

items.q: Kai turns a rectangular floor tile (not a square) a quarter turn. Will it look the same as before?
c: No, it needs a half turn
No, only after a full turn
items.e: After a quarter turn the long sides point the other way, so it looks different. A rectangle looks the same after a half turn (order 2). Having mirror lines does not tell you about turns.

items.q: Mei says the capital letter N has a line of symmetry, because it looks the same upside down. Is she right?
c: No, N has no symmetry at all
items.e: Looking the same after a half turn is rotational symmetry (order 2). No fold of N makes the halves match, so it has 0 lines of symmetry.
